name: SEYCHELLES

flag.title: Flag of Seychelles
flag.note: Five rays of blue, yellow, red, white, green

lead: Seychelles is a tiny nation of 115 islands in the Indian Ocean. Round granite boulders sit in turquoise water. Over half the land is protected, and giant tortoises outnumber people.

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: Seychelles lies alone in the Indian Ocean, about 1,500 km east of Africa. Mahé, the biggest island, has the capital Victoria and 90% of all residents.
The outer islands are flat coral rings called atolls. Remote Aldabra is a UNESCO World Heritage site. The sea around Seychelles covers over 1.3 million km².
animals: The Aldabra giant tortoise is the symbol of Seychelles. Over 100,000 live on Aldabra Atoll. They weigh up to 250 kg and live past 150 years.
The Seychelles black parrot, called kato nwar, lives only on Praslin. About 1,000 are left. Green sea turtles nest on quiet beaches.
culture: Seychellois culture mixes African, French, Indian and Chinese roots. This mix is called Creole. Meals include grilled fish with chilli-ginger sauce and octopus curry. Festival Kreol fills the streets each October.
Moutya is a song and dance born from the chants of enslaved people. People sing it around beach bonfires. Sega has bongo drums and a hip-swaying shuffle.
history: No one lived on the islands until 1770. Then French settlers came with enslaved Africans to plant spices. Britain took over in 1810. Independence came peacefully on 29 June 1976.
Pirate Olivier le Vasseur, called 'La Buse' (the Buzzard), is said to have buried treasure here. He was executed in 1730. Nobody has solved his coded riddle.
wows: Seychelles' inner islands are Earth's only mid-ocean granite islands, not volcanic or coral.
The coco de mer palm grows the world's largest seed, up to 25 kg, heavy as a child.
Over 50% of Seychelles is protected, the highest share of any country.
You can walk across Victoria's city centre in under ten minutes.
The Seychelles magpie-robin fell to 16 birds in the 1960s, then recovered to 300+.
No venomous snakes live on any Seychelles island.
Seychelles controls an ocean zone nearly 3,000 times bigger than its land.

myths.myth: A tortoise can climb out of its shell
myths.fact: The shell is part of the tortoise's body. Its ribs and backbone are joined to it.

myths.myth: Pirates made people walk the plank
myths.fact: There is almost no proof that pirates did this. The idea mostly comes from stories and films.
